XV.|OF THE APOSTLES.|335}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=15|verse=22}}† Then it plea{{ls}}ed the Apo{{ls}}tles and Auncients vvith the vvhole Church, to cho{{ls}}e men out of them, & to {{ls}}end to Antioche vvith Paul and Barnabas, Iudas, vvho vvas {{ls}}urnamed Bar{{ls}}abas, & Silas, cheefe men among the brethren, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Other latin copies and the greeke read thus, ''Writing by their handes an epi{{ls}}tle conteining the{{ls}}e things''.}}∷ vvriting by their handes.

The Apo{{ls}}tles and Auncients, the brethren, to the brethren of the Gentiles that are at Antioche and in Syria and Cilicia, greeting. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=24}}† Becau{{ls}}e vve haue heard that certaine {{sup|‖}} going forth from vs, haue troubled you vvith vvordes, {{ls}}ubuerting your {{ls}}oules, to vvhom vve gaue no commaundement: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=25}}† it hath plea{{ls}}ed vs being gathered in one, to cho{{ls}}e out men and to {{ls}}end them vnto you vvith our deere{{ls}}t Barnabas and Paul, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=26}}† men that haue giuen their liues for the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=27}}† We haue {{ls}}ent therfore Iudas & Silas, vvho them {{ls}}elues al{{ls}}o wil in vvordes report vnto you the {{ls}}ame things. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=28}}† For it hath {{ls}}eemed good {{sup|‖}} to the holy Gho{{ls}}t & to vs, to lay no further burden vpon you then the{{ls}}e nece{{ls}}sarie things: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=29}}† that you ab{{ls}}teine from the things immolated to Idols, and bloud, and that vvhich is {{ls}}trangled, and {{sup|‖}} fornication, from the vvhich things keeping your {{ls}}elues, you {{ls}}hal doe vvell. Fare ye vvel.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=30}}† They therfore being dimi{{ls}}sed went downe to Antioche: and gathering the multitude, deliuered the epi{{ls}}tle. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=31}}† Vvhich vvhen they had read, they {{sup|‖}} reioyced vpon the con{{ls}}olation: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=32}}† but Iudas and Silas, them Selues al{{ls}}o being prophets, vvith many vvordes comforted the brethren, and confirmed them. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=33}}† And hauing {{ls}}pent {{ls}}ome time there, they vvere vvith peace dimi{{ls}}sed of the brethren vnto them that had {{ls}}ent them. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=34}}† But it {{ls}}eemed good vnto Silas to remaine there: and Iudas departed alone: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=35}}† and Paul and Barnabas taried at Antioche, teaching and euangelizing vvith many others the vvord of our Lord.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=36}}† And after certaine daies, Paul {{ls}}aid to Barnabas, Let vs returne and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 13, 14.''}}* vi{{ls}}ite our brethren in al cities vvherein vve {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Hereof our Catholike Bi{{ls}}hops tooke vp the nece{{ls}}sarie v{{ls}}e of often vi{{ls}}iting their flockes & cures committed to their charge, for confirmation in faith & vertue, & reformation of maners both of clergie & laitie. · Act. 13, 14.}}∷ haue preached the vvord of our Lord, how they doe. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=37}}† And Barnabas vvould haue taken vvith them Iohn al{{ls}}o that vvas {{ls}}urnamed Marke. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=38}}† But Paul de{{ls}}ired that he (as vvho {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 13, 13.''}}* had departed from them out of Pamphylia, and had not gone vvith them to the vvorke) might not be receiued. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=39}}† And there ro{{ls}}e a {{sup|‖}} di{{ls}}{{ls}}ention, {{ls}}o that they departed one from an other, & that Barnabas in deede taking Marke {{ls}}ailed to Cypres. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=40}}† But<noinclude>{{rh|||Paul}}</noinclude>
